subject: PrivDeploy pricing: crediting vs annualized SKU construct
messages:
From: Rebecca Liu <rebecca.liu@nebulahealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@nebulahealth.com>, procurement@nebulahealth.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 16:15:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment pricing questions and SKU crediting

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the performance numbers look promising. Procurement and engineering have a few follow-ups focused on the commercial structure for a VPC/on-prem deployment. The main ask is to understand the trade-offs between:

- Annualized SKU commitments (committed nodes/GPUs, annual prepay) with a lower platform fee vs
- A smaller committed SKU + platform fee amortization and discrete implementation credits during rollout.

We attached our list of questions (Nebula_Questions_v3.xlsx) — highlights: whether platform fee is refundable or creditable against node spend, how support tiers map to response windows for on-prem incidents, and whether we can structure an early-adopter starter tranche with reduced fees for the first 6 months.

Can you send a clear comparison table and an example TCO for 12/24/36 month profiles? Also include any ramp credits you’ve done previously for similar healthcare customers.

Best,
Rebecca
Director, ML Platforms
Nebula Health

Attachment: Nebula_Questions_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet stub, 12 rows)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Liu <rebecca.liu@nebulahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 18:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing questions and SKU crediting

Hi Rebecca — thanks for the thoughtful list and for sharing the spreadsheet. I looped in Ben (pricing) and Jordan (solutions) so we can put a crisp comparison together. Quick answers up-front:

- Platform fee: typically a non-refundable recurring fee that covers the private control plane, licensing, and baseline observability; however, we can offer one-time implementation credits (or a transient reduced platform fee) for a staged roll-out.
- Crediting: we can apply implementation credits against your first two quarters of node invoices (not as a cash refund) or convert them to additional committed capacity at quote time.
- Support: our Standard/Enhanced/Premier tiers have defined SLOs; for on-prem we often recommend Enhanced (4-hour P1) for production LLM inference.

Ben and Jordan — could you draft two concrete price scenarios (A = heavier annual SKU prepay with lower platform fee; B = lower prepay + larger platform fee but with implementation credits that vest across month 0–6)? Rebecca, we’ll aim to get a 12/24/36-month TCO and an example term sheet by Friday.

Thanks,
Priya
Head of Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

---
Note: Attachment referenced by customer remains in their email.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rebecca Liu <rebecca.liu@nebulahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing questions and SKU crediting -- initial scenarios

Team — drafting two compact scenarios below. I’ll produce a spreadsheet and a one-pager for Rebecca. Notes in-line:

Scenario A — Annualized SKU (Anchor)
- Commit: 24 x reserved nodes (NVIDIA H100-equivalent) annual prepay (invoiced quarterly)
- Platform fee: $40k / month (reduced rate due to commit)
- Support: Enhanced included; Premier add-on at +15% of platform fee
- Credits: 10% implementation credit applied as invoice credit across first 2 invoices
- Pros: predictable unit pricing, capacity reservation for spikes
- Cons: higher upfront commit, less flexibility for burst/region failover

Scenario B — Hybrid (Lower Commit + Amortized Platform)
- Commit: 8 x reserved nodes, metered burst to hosted pool
- Platform fee: $85k / month (covers private control plane + higher ops retainer)
- Implementation credits: $120k applied as invoice credits month 0–6 (30%/30%/20%/20%)
- Support: Enhanced included; Premier available with 30-day pilot at reduced rate
- Pros: lower capex, credits soften early-year costs, easier exit after 12 months
- Cons: higher steady-state platform fee unless converted to larger commit in year 2

Ask: Priya — do we want to show an alternate where platform fee is amortized and converted to node credits if Nebula upsizes above 16 nodes in year 2? That is a common concession.

Ben
Senior Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: draft-pricing-scenarios.csv (stub)

From: Rebecca Liu <rebecca.liu@nebulahealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@nebulahealth.com>, procurement@nebulahealth.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 13:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing questions and SKU crediting -- clarifications from procurement

Thanks Ben — these are helpful. Procurement has a few follow-ups so we can run internal approvals: 

1) Can implementation credits be structured as a true rebate on the node line (so it appears in our run-rate calculations) rather than only as a platform invoice offset?
2) We need a worked example that shows cashflow timing (invoices and credits) and the net effective price per GPU-hour at 50%/75%/100% utilization.
3) What are the guaranteed patching and security update windows in the Enhanced tier for a healthcare customer (SOC2 evidence required)?

On the early-adopter tranche: Nebula is open to a starter pilot (3–6 months) with a capped node count if we can get a 6-month reduced platform fee and a pathway to convert credits to committed nodes.

Can you also include a clause showing what happens at month 12 if utilization is >120% of committed capacity (automatic burst pricing vs negotiated uplift)? Procurement prefers an automatic uplift formula rather than ad-hoc renegotiation.

Best,
Rebecca

Attachment: none

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: suggested contract language and security notes

Internal note — copying key points I’ll add to the term sheet: 
- Credit treatment: propose we allow credits to be posted as "Implementation Credits" on the node line for the first 6 months; they reduce net invoiceable node units and are visible in Nebula's run-rate model (satisfies procurement ask #1).
- Conversion mechanism: credits convert to additional committed nodes at the quoted list price less the applied credit amount; conversion window months 6–18.
- Burst clause: automatic burst surcharge = list-burst-rate * (utilization / committed) for any sustained monthly average >110% (with a cap at 200% uplift).
- SOC2 / Patching: Enhanced tier includes monthly security patch windows and weekly audit log exports; for healthcare customers we can include quarterly independent attestations at cost.

I’ll draft the redlines for the contract team and push a version to the HubSpot deal record. Ben — can you finalize the sample TCO spreadsheet and I’ll drop the proposed contract language into the term sheet?

Jordan
Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Liu <rebecca.liu@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 17:43:00 -08:00
Subject: Private deployment: consolidated commercial options and next steps

Rebecca — attached is a concise packet (Redwood_PrivDeploy_Tiered_Pricing_v2.pdf) with:
- Side-by-side 12/24/36 month TCOs for Scenarios A and B
- Cashflow timing tables showing invoice dates and applied credits
- Proposed contract language for crediting, conversion window, and burst surcharge formula
- Support tier matrix including Enhanced SLOs and SOC2 evidence options

Highlights tailored to Nebula:
- Starter tranche: 6-month reduced platform fee of 50% off for the first 6 months if Nebula commits to a 12-month minimum and agrees to convert any unused implementation credits to committed nodes in months 6–18.
- Credit visibility: Implementation credits will appear on the node invoice line for run-rate purposes (per procurement ask).
- Upsize protection: If monthly utilization >120% sustained for 2 consecutive months, automatic burst uplift triggers per formula; the parties may negotiate conversion to committed nodes with credit conversion options.

Next steps: 1) Review the PDF; 2) Procurement to confirm preferred cashflow treatment and pilot node cap; 3) If agreeable, we’ll issue an updated term sheet and a redlineable SOW for legal review.

I’m available early next week for a 30-minute call to walk through the TCO and the conversion mechanics.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_PrivDeploy_Tiered_Pricing_v2.pdf (pricing packet), Nebula_Questions_v3.xlsx (customer supplied)
